research: Spread-specific: Alabama opened -6.5 and moved through 7 to -8.5 at some books, with Alabama drawing what WagerTalk called '100 percent of the money and tickets from the start' (WagerTalk preview, Oct 2026). The move came with the public, not against it. Our slate line, -7.5 at -112, sits in the middle of that move. This is a weak argument for Tennessee if you think the public inflated it; per LESSONS, no further bet in the direction of the move.
Spread-specific: Bill Connelly's SP+ projects Alabama by only 3.8, nearly five points off the market's -8.5 (Predictem preview, Oct 2026). Helps Tennessee +7.5.
Spread-specific: Covers' Rob Paul takes Alabama -7.5 and says he'd play it up to -9.5. Kalshi prices Alabama at about 74% to win outright (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Helps Alabama.

Tennessee QB: George MacIntyre makes his second straight start. He had a 10.3 QBR in his first, a 7-point win at Arkansas with 2 INTs, and has a 24.7 QBR on the season. Tennessee is 128th nationally in pass success rate (33.8%) (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Helps Alabama: the underdog's ability to score is in doubt.

[angle] True freshman QB Faizon Brandon (shoulder) was back at practice Tuesday, and Heupel wouldn't name a starter ('We'll find out here through the week'), so both QBs could play (Predictem citing On3, Oct 2026). The QB uncertainty cuts both ways.

Tennessee's strength is the run: No. 2 in EPA per rush, and DeSean Bishop has 678 yards and 8 TDs, top 10 in yards after contact (Covers; Predictem, Oct 2026). But Alabama is 9th in defensive rush success rate (35.4%) (Covers). The matchup favors Alabama.

Alabama's offense: Keelon Russell is 3rd nationally in QBR (90.0), with 80.9+ in four straight games before Georgia. Alabama is No. 2 in net adjusted EPA/play and 4th in rush success rate (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Helps Alabama.

[angle] Alabama comes off its first loss, 20-17 at home to Georgia, where Russell had a career-low completion rate and was sacked four times (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 2026). WR Ryan Coleman-Williams (head/knee) is expected out (DeBoer, per Predictem). Slightly helps Tennessee.

Tennessee's defense under Jim Knowles allows 15.5 points per game and has more interceptions than TD passes allowed. Tennessee's last four games all stayed under the total (Predictem; WagerTalk, Oct 2026). A low-scoring game helps the +7.5 side.

[angle] The home team has won and covered each of the last five meetings, and Alabama's 2020 win was the last by a road team in Knoxville (WagerTalk; Predictem, Oct 2026). This is old history, so little weight. Helps Tennessee.

Tennessee's form: lost by 3 at home to then-No. 1 Texas, then beat Auburn and Arkansas (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Opponents score on 94% of red-zone trips vs Alabama, one of the 20 worst rates in FBS (Predictem). Helps Tennessee keep it close.
games.reasoning: SP+ (Alabama by 3.8) and Tennessee's defense point to Tennessee +7.5. Tennessee's broken passing game (128th in pass success, a 10.3 QBR from MacIntyre) and Alabama's top-10 run defense against Tennessee's one strength point the other way. Shading my projection halfway to the line gives about Alabama by 6.5, within 2 points of 7.5, so pass. The surprising angle is the QB uncertainty: Brandon was back at practice and Heupel wouldn't name a starter. A confirmed Brandon start, or the line reaching 9+, would have made Tennessee a lean.

research: Spread-specific: Georgia opened -18.5 and moved to -20.5 even though Auburn had 65% of the money, with tickets split 50-50 (WagerTalk, Oct 14 2026). That is reverse movement toward the favorite, a signal LESSONS says has not worked (0-2). Our slate line is -19.5.
Spread-specific: Dimers' model projects Georgia 35, Auburn 15 and gives Georgia only 51.6% to cover -18.5 (Dimers, Oct 2026). At 19.5 the model is a coin flip or slightly toward Auburn.
Spread-specific: Georgia is 6-0 SU and 5-1 ATS, its only miss a 2-point win over Vanderbilt. Auburn is 1-4 ATS (WagerTalk, Oct 14 2026). LESSONS treats team ATS records as noise, so tiebreaker only.
Georgia beat Alabama by 3 on the road in Week 6, with +109 net yards and +6:56 time of possession. No 2026 opponent has scored more than 20 points on Georgia (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Helps Georgia.
Auburn's offense is weak: 14 points and 17 first downs in the loss at Tennessee, and 21 points and 279 yards vs Vanderbilt (Covers, Oct 17 2026). A 19.5-point underdog needs to score. Helps Georgia.
[angle] Auburn will be without preseason All-American LB Xavier Atkins (Alex Golesh, per WagerTalk, Oct 14 2026). Helps Georgia.
[angle] First-year coach Alex Golesh hasn't been able to run his fast tempo; many players who followed him from South Florida aren't yet SEC-ready (WagerTalk, Oct 14 2026). Helps Georgia.
[angle] Possible letdown spot: Georgia comes off a physical road win at Alabama, and WagerTalk says Auburn is off a bye (WagerTalk, Oct 14 2026). Helps Auburn.
Weather: gusts up to 20 mph could limit downfield passing (Covers, Oct 17 2026). A lower-scoring game slightly helps the big underdog, but per LESSONS this isn't counted as a separate reason.

History: Georgia has won 9 straight vs Auburn (7-2 ATS since the 2017 SEC title game) and held Auburn to 286.1 yards per game in that run. It won 20-10 at Auburn last season (WagerTalk, Oct 14 2026). Old history, low weight. Helps Georgia.

Covers' top pick is Georgia -20.5 (54% playable), and it likes Georgia -10.5 in the first half (Covers, Oct 17 2026). WagerTalk takes Auburn +20.5 and projects 38-20 (WagerTalk). Expert opinion is split.
games.reasoning: The models (Dimers 35-15) and the market sit on top of the 19.5 line. Auburn's inability to score argues for Georgia, while Georgia's own modest scoring (20 points vs Alabama) and the letdown spot argue for Auburn, so this is a pass. The most interesting angle is the move toward Georgia against Auburn money, which LESSONS says not to follow. A clear Auburn QB or line injury would have tipped it to Georgia.

research: Spread-specific: SP+ ranks Missouri a few spots above Ole Miss and has Ole Miss favored by less than half a point, vs a 5.5-6 point market (Predictem, Oct 2026). This is the main support for Missouri +5.5.

Spread-specific: ESPN's matchup predictor gives Ole Miss about 58%, while the moneyline implies about 66% (Predictem; Covers, Oct 2026). The market is a bit more bullish on Ole Miss than the models are. Helps Missouri.

Spread-specific: lines ranged from Ole Miss -4.5 (Dimers) to -6 (Predictem) to -6.5 at one Covers consensus snapshot, with about 51% of picks on Missouri. Dimers' model projects 31-26 Ole Miss, a 5-point margin. Mixed: the market hasn't moved decisively either way.

Missouri's defense allows 2.3 yards per carry (4th nationally), Missouri is top 10 in turnover margin, and it held Texas A&M to 6 points last week and beat Florida by four TDs (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Missouri.
Ole Miss's defense ranks outside the top 50 in SP+ and in the bottom third in EPA/play allowed. Florida scored 50+ on it in Gainesville (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Missouri.

[angle] Missouri QB Austin Simmons is the former Ole Miss starter: he lost the job when he was hurt at Kentucky in 2025 and Trinidad Chambliss took over, then transferred. He has 14 TD passes and 1 INT this season (Predictem, Oct 2026). A revenge spot against his old team helps Missouri.

Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss is a dual-threat Heisman contender, and Ole Miss's offense is top 10 in SP+. It scored TDs on 4 of its first 5 drives vs Vanderbilt (Covers; Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Ole Miss.

Missouri's red-zone offense scores on only about 75% of trips, one of the worst rates in FBS (Predictem, Oct 2026). Missouri also allowed 31 points and 499 yards at Mississippi State, its one road game vs a ranked team (Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Ole Miss.

[angle] Ole Miss DB Edwin Joseph sprained an ankle at Vanderbilt and was getting a second opinion. Pete Golding called him 'the only concern right now from an injury standpoint' (Predictem, Oct 2026). Slightly helps Missouri.

Ole Miss has been volatile: 4-1, with wins over Louisville and LSU, then a blowout loss at Florida right after the emotional LSU (Lane Kiffin return) game (Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Missouri; Ole Miss is not a steady margin team.
[angle] Ole Miss hasn't beaten Missouri since 1974, a motivation point for the Rebels (Covers, Oct 2026). Old history, low weight. Helps Ole Miss.
Missouri is 8-9 ATS as an SEC road underdog under Drinkwitz (Covers citing Phil Steele, Oct 2026). Neutral noise. Wind gusts near 20 mph forecast (Covers).
games.reasoning: The deciding numbers are SP+ (nearly a pick'em) against a 5.5-point line, plus Missouri's elite run defense and turnover margin against an Ole Miss defense in the bottom third by EPA. Shading halfway toward the line still leaves Ole Miss by about 3, so Missouri +5.5 is a lean. The surprising angle is Austin Simmons, the former Ole Miss starter, returning to Oxford. Clear money moving the line to 6.5+ toward Ole Miss, or Missouri's bad red-zone offense, are why this isn't strong.

research: Spread-specific: Miami opened -21 and moved between -20.5 and -21.5, sitting at -21.5 by game week, with 97% of the money and 75% of tickets on Miami (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Heavy Miami support barely moved the line, which WagerTalk reads as respect for FSU. Our slate line is Miami -20.5, with FSU +20.5 juiced to -150, consistent with a market number near 21.5.
Spread-specific: Dimers projects Miami 38-18 (a 20-point margin, 93.9% win probability) at -20.5 (Dimers, Oct 2026). That's essentially on the line.
Spread-specific: Miami is 5-0 SU and 4-1 ATS (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Noise per LESSONS.
Miami's offense averages 42.8 points per game vs FBS, 8.2 yards per play and an 83% completion rate. QB Darian Mensah has 15 TDs and 0 INTs (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Helps Miami.
FSU has allowed 47.0 points per game in two road games, ranks 116th in adjusted defensive EPA, and allows 6.1 yards per play (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Helps Miami.
[angle] FSU collapsed at Louisville last week: nearly up 21-0 before a goal-line stop, then outscored 44-6 over the final 39 minutes, a 24-point loss (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps Miami.

[angle] Miami comes off a bye after beating Clemson, and expects edge Marquise Lightfoot, CBs Xavier Lucas and Damari Brown, and LB Ezekiel Marcelin back from early-season injuries (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Helps Miami.
[angle] Miami OL Max Buchanan is expected to miss the next few weeks with a knee injury (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Slightly helps FSU.

Rivalry margins have often frustrated favorites: Miami won by 1 as a 14-point favorite (2018), FSU covered as a 22.5-point underdog (2024), and Miami won only 28-22 in Tallahassee last season (WagerTalk, Oct 2026). Old history, low weight. Helps FSU.
Weather: thunderstorms and heavy rain are likely, which could favor the run game (Covers, Oct 17 2026). Not counted as a separate reason per LESSONS.
FSU played Alabama and SMU relatively close earlier this season, and averages 14.3 yards per completion (Covers, Oct 17 2026). FSU can create explosive plays for a backdoor. Helps FSU.
Expert picks: Covers takes FSU only at +21.5 or more, and WagerTalk takes FSU +21.5 and projects 34-17 (Covers; WagerTalk, Oct 2026). At our 20.5, a point worse for FSU, both are near indifference.
games.reasoning: Miami's offensive efficiency, its returning defenders after a bye and FSU's road defense (47 PPG allowed) favor Miami. The rivalry's history of close margins and the rain favor FSU. The models and market sit right at 20.5-21.5, so this is a pass. The notable angle is FSU's 44-6 collapse after nearly leading Louisville 21-0. A confirmed Miami secondary return plus a line at 19 or lower would have made Miami a lean.

research: Spread-specific: SP+ has Houston by 4.4, essentially the 4.5 line (Predictem, Oct 2026). This argues for a pass.

Spread-specific: the spread moved a full point toward Houston since the open, while about 65% of Covers consensus picks are on Oklahoma State (Predictem, Oct 2026). That is reverse movement toward the favorite, which LESSONS says has not been useful (0-2). Slightly helps Houston at most.
Spread-specific: Houston is 1-3 ATS when favored, and Oklahoma State is 4-1 ATS on a four-game win streak (Predictem, Oct 2026). Noise per LESSONS; at most a tiebreaker toward Oklahoma State.
Dimers' model projects Houston 32-28 with a 63.9% win probability (Dimers, Oct 2026), a 4-point margin. On the line.
Houston leads FBS in third-down conversion (58.2%) and is 4th in success rate (~53%). Oklahoma State converts only 30.8% on third down (Predictem citing TeamRankings, Oct 2026). Helps Houston.
Houston allows only 74 rushing yards per game, while Oklahoma State RB Caleb Hawkins averages about 105 a game (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Houston.

[angle] Eric Morris rebuilt a 1-11 Oklahoma State team with 91 newcomers, possibly a record in major college football, and has it ranked No. 18 on a 4-game win streak with 40+ points in three straight (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Oklahoma State: its strength may be underrated.
[angle] Houston's red-zone defense allows scores on 92.9% of trips (Predictem, Oct 2026). With a 62.5 total, that opens backdoor-cover risk. Helps Oklahoma State.

[angle] Houston coach Willie Fritz said the Cougars 'can compete for a national championship.' Houston beat Kansas State 35-16 on the road last week, with 4 TD passes from Conner Weigman (Predictem; SportsGambler, Oct 2026). Helps Houston.
QBs: Weigman has 15 TDs and 1 INT, Mestemaker 13 TDs and 5 INTs (Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Houston.
Injuries: Houston RB JayShon Ridgle is questionable; Oklahoma State guard J. Sexton and TE O. Hammond are out (Predictem, Oct 2026). Slightly helps Houston.
games.reasoning: SP+ (4.4) and Dimers (4) both put this right on the 4.5 line. Houston's third-down and run-defense edges are offset by its leaky red zone and Oklahoma State's scoring streak in a game with a 62.5 total, so pass. The surprising angle is Oklahoma State's 91-newcomer rebuild under Eric Morris. A firm line at 3.5 or a confirmed Ridgle absence would have changed the calculus.

research: Spread-specific: the line moved through the key number of 10 to Notre Dame -10.5 (some books -11), from earlier numbers around -9.5 (Covers expert panel; Predictem, Oct 2026). The move followed BYU losing RB LJ Martin. Per LESSONS, an injury-driven move is information: don't add to it or fade it.

Spread-specific: Kalshi priced Notre Dame -10.5 at 51% and BYU +10.5 at 50%, a coin flip at the number (Covers, Oct 2026). Dimers projects 29-19 Notre Dame (Dimers, Oct 2026), 10 points, essentially on the line.

Spread-specific: BYU is 8-1 ATS (7-2 SU) in its last nine as a home underdog, and Notre Dame is 19-9-2 ATS in its last 30 as a road favorite (Predictem, Oct 2026). These cancel out, and LESSONS treats them as noise anyway.

BYU's leading rusher LJ Martin (344 yards in four games) is out at least a month with a leg injury, and RB Sione Moa is out for the season. Backups Tonga and Rex had 40 yards on 14 carries vs Iowa State (Predictem; Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Notre Dame, but it's priced.

Notre Dame is No. 1 nationally in net success rate and net EPA per play. It allows 11.0 points and 58.3 rushing yards per game and has allowed one rushing TD all season (Covers; Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps Notre Dame against BYU's run-based QB game.

[angle] Notre Dame hasn't faced a ranked team or a hostile road environment this season (Sagarin schedule rank 31). Provo is a night game, and BYU is 39-8 SU in its last 47 at home (Covers; Predictem, Oct 2026). Helps BYU.
[angle] BYU has been outscored 98-20 in three games vs top-10 opponents over four years (Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Notre Dame.

BYU's offense: QB Bear Bachmeier has 8 passing TDs, 1 INT, 4 rushing TDs and over 200 rushing yards. BYU scored only 24 vs Iowa State and 17 at TCU in recent weeks (Predictem; Covers, Oct 2026). A double-digit underdog needs to score, which helps Notre Dame.
BYU's defense allows only 13.4 points per game but ranks 78th in EPA per rush, and Jonaz Walton has 301 rushing yards in his last two games (Covers, Oct 2026). Helps Notre Dame.

[angle] Notre Dame is first nationally in fewest penalties (~3 a game), and CJ Carr has a 16-1 TD-INT ratio. CB Leonard Moore is questionable after a concussion (Predictem, Oct 2026). Mostly helps Notre Dame.
Low total of 46.5-47.5, with experts split on the over and under (Covers, Oct 2026). Not counted as a reason for the underdog per LESSONS.
Expert panel: Powers (own number 13) and Rob Paul take Notre Dame -10.5, Predictem's Mann takes Notre Dame -9.5, and Marchio and Covers' AI take BYU +10.5 (Covers; Predictem, Oct 2026).
games.reasoning: Notre Dame's efficiency profile and BYU's depleted backfield favor the Irish. But the line already moved through 10 on the Martin injury, and LESSONS says not to bet further in the direction of an injury move. Kalshi and Dimers both sit on the number, so pass. The most interesting angle is that this is Notre Dame's first ranked opponent and first hostile road night game. A line back at 9.5 would have made Notre Dame a lean.
